identity_evidence.quote: A woman in her early 50s with rheumatoid arthritis presented with a three-day history of epigastric pain, vomiting, and melena.

attribution_limitations: The text says "oral methotrexate and methylprednisolone" for the home medications; it is unclear whether "oral" covers both drugs.

The differential diagnosis lists peptic ulcer disease and acute pancreatitis with a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm and then says the features were absent; no explicit "excluded" wording is given for either diagnosis.

Rheumatoid vasculitis is described as "suggested" and the "probable underlying cause", while the discussion also says the diagnosis was established after ruling out other causes; it is not stated as biopsy or test proven.
The white blood cell count after treatment is printed "6.500/µL" with a decimal point, while the admission count is printed 12,800/µL.

The text does not give the time of the examination, imaging, endoscopy or laboratory tests other than hemoglobin and white blood cell count relative to admission, and does not state when the corticosteroid and methotrexate were started relative to the embolization.
The pain relief is placed "within two days of conservative treatment" and the discharge "on day 4 post-procedure"; the conservative treatment is not defined.
The abstract and conclusion describe coil embolization as effective for hemodynamically stable patients; the case text states no hemodynamic status for this patient.
The two-month follow-up has no stated reference point (discharge or procedure), and "post-procedure" and "The procedure" are not tied to a named procedure beyond the embolization context.
